channel.title: Frontion - Global Headlines
channel.description: Breaking geopolitical headlines curated from Tier 1 sources worldwide

item.title: Pentagon Quietly Removes 4 US Troop Deaths From Iran War Casualty Count
item.description: The Pentagon revised its official Iran war casualty database, removing four troops previously listed as killed during renewed fighting. The total wounded count simultaneously grew by over 140, pushing casualties past 600 since the conflict began.

item.title: Saudi Arabia Shoots Down Iranian Drones Targeting Oil Facilities as Regional Attacks Spread
item.description: Saudi Arabia, Jordan, and Iraq all reported drone attacks hours after the US paused its bombing campaign against Iran. Saudi forces intercepted drones heading toward oil facilities, testing the fragile ceasefire.

item.title: China Accuses US of AI Hegemonism, Threatens Countermeasures Over Sanctions Threat
item.description: China's commerce ministry accused the US of "AI hegemonism" and warned of countermeasures after Washington threatened sanctions against Chinese AI firms over alleged technology theft through distillation.

item.title: Zelenskyy Meets UK PM Burnham as Britain Unveils Stone Cloak Support Package for Ukraine
item.description: Ukrainian President Zelenskyy visited a naval base in Portsmouth to meet Prime Minister Andy Burnham, who unveiled the Stone Cloak military support package for Ukraine amid intensifying drone attacks and the widening Iran-Ukraine row.

item.title: France Says Monster Wildfire That Forced 250,000 to Flee Has Stopped Growing
item.description: French President Macron held a crisis meeting as the massive Gironde wildfire that forced over 250,000 evacuations near Bordeaux stabilized. Spain reported progress containing two major blazes near Madrid.

item.title: Pentagon quietly revises Iran war casualty figures as 624+ US troops wounded
item.description: The Pentagon has revised its official casualty data from the Iran war, reducing the death toll for Operation Epic Fury from 18 to 14 by moving four fallen soldiers to a new Overseas Operations category starting July 7. At least 624 US service members have been wounded since February, drawing bipartisan criticism over transparency.

item.title: Mediators see progress in US-Iran diplomacy as drone attacks rattle Saudi Arabia, Jordan and Iraq
item.description: Regional mediators have made progress in efforts to bring the US and Iran back to negotiations after Trump paused air strikes. Meanwhile, drone attacks hit Iran's neighbors — Saudi Arabia, Jordan and Iraq — in what appears to be Tehran testing the latest pause in hostilities.

item.title: Israel approves limited international stabilization force in Gaza with 200 troops for Rafah
item.description: Israel's security cabinet has approved a scaled-back pilot deployment of 200 troops from Morocco and Uganda to a designated zone in Rafah, part of Trump's 20-point peace plan. Analysts call it a calculated diplomatic gesture to deflect US pressure ahead of Netanyahu's Washington visit, with little practical effect on the ground.

item.title: Australian court rejects Pauline Hanson appeal over racial discrimination against Muslim senator
item.description: A three-judge panel of Australia's Federal Court unanimously dismissed One Nation leader Pauline Hanson's appeal against a ruling that she racially discriminated against Greens Senator Mehreen Faruqi by telling her to "pack your bags" and leave Australia. Hanson said she intends to appeal to the High Court.

item.title: Iran Claims Control of Strait of Hormuz, Says It Is Not Seeking Talks After US Bombing Halt
item.description: Iran stated it still controls the strategic Strait of Hormuz and is not seeking new negotiations with the US, despite Trump pausing 13 consecutive nights of strikes to allow diplomatic space. The standoff leaves global oil shipping routes in limbo.

item.title: Deadly Van Attack Near Berlin Pride Festival Raises Security Questions
item.description: A woman was killed and at least 16 injured when a van rammed into a crowd near Berlin's Pride festival. Germany's interior minister called it a suspected Islamic extremist terror attack. Questions are mounting over why the suspect had been released from custody.

item.title: Saudi Arabia Intercepts Iranian-Backed Militia Drones Targeting Oil Facilities
item.description: Saudi air defenses intercepted and destroyed several drones launched from Iraq by Iran-backed militias targeting the kingdom's petroleum facilities. Saudi Arabia condemned the attacks and reserved the right to respond, as regional tensions escalate alongside the US-Iran conflict.

item.title: Oil Prices Plunge 7% as US-Iran Pause Strikes for Diplomacy
item.description: Brent crude fell below $90 a barrel and US crude dropped to around $83 — both down roughly 7% — after the US and Iran paused their escalating strikes to allow room for diplomacy. Global stock markets rallied on hopes the conflict could de-escalate.

item.title: Wildfires Force Mass Evacuations Across France and Spain as Fire Clouds Form
item.description: More than 250,000 people have been evacuated in southwestern France as wildfires approach Bordeaux, while Spain battles blazes near Madrid and Castellón. Pyrocumulonimbus clouds — fire-generated thunderstorms — are intensifying the fires, with King Felipe VI visiting evacuation centers.

item.title: UK selects Tekever AR5 surveillance drones to replace Watchkeeper fleet
item.description: The UK Ministry of Defence has chosen Portuguese-made Tekever AR5 drones to succeed the troubled Watchkeeper program, marking a shift toward lighter, more flexible ISR capabilities for the British Army.

item.title: Indonesia central bank governor Warjiyo resigns as rupiah hits record lows
item.description: Bank Indonesia Governor Perry Warjiyo stepped down before his term expires, following mounting criticism over the rupiah's plunge to record lows and accelerating capital flight from Southeast Asia's largest economy.

item.title: Mediators report progress on diplomatic opening to de-escalate US-Iran conflict
item.description: Qatar and Pakistan-led mediation efforts have made progress toward resuming US-Iran negotiations, with regional officials saying both sides appear open to a diplomatic off-ramp after 13 nights of strikes.

item.title: US criticism of Malaysia Israel ban spotlights growing diplomatic disconnect
item.description: US accusations that Malaysia's ban on Israelis entering the country is antisemitic are unlikely to change policy but underscore widening diplomatic rifts between Washington and Muslim-majority Southeast Asian nations.

item.title: Marcos pushes tax exemptions and power reforms to revive Philippine growth
item.description: Philippine President Marcos Jr. used his penultimate State of the Nation Address to propose raising income tax thresholds and energy reforms, aiming to stimulate an economy hit by the global oil crisis.

item.title: Oil prices plunge over 9% as US-Iran pause raises de-escalation hopes
item.description: Brent crude fell below $88 a barrel after the US halted attacks on Iran for a second consecutive night and Iran paused retaliatory strikes, sparking market optimism about a diplomatic resolution to the conflict.

item.title: Iran warns Ukraine of retaliation after deadly Caspian Sea strike on vessel
item.description: Iran Foreign Minister Araghchi said a Ukrainian attack on an Iranian commercial vessel in the Caspian Sea that killed one sailor cannot go unanswered, accusing Israel of provoking the strike to drag Europe into a wider conflict.

item.title: US appeals court upholds halt to Trump executive order creating federal voter list
item.description: A federal appeals court upheld a lower court ruling blocking Trump's order to create a federal citizenship list for voters and restrict mail ballot delivery, rejecting the administration's effort to implement it ahead of the November midterms.

item.title: Ukrainian startup Fire Point mass-producing cruise missiles, striking deep into Russia
item.description: The Guardian reports Fire Point is manufacturing 100 Flamingo cruise missiles monthly and hundreds of drones daily, enabling Ukraine to sustain deep-strike operations inside Russia and closing the gap on Russian long-range attack capabilities.

item.title: Argentina Milei calls Brazil Lula a thief and convict at Bolsonaro campaign rally
item.description: Argentina president Javier Milei insulted Brazilian president Lula da Silva at a rally for Flavio Bolsonaro in Sao Paulo, prompting Brazil to recall its ambassador and escalating a diplomatic crisis between South America two largest economies.

item.title: US Congress approves $500M for Taiwan defense as Trump continues hesitating on arms package
item.description: The US House passed a bill including $500 million in Foreign Military Financing for Taiwan, signaling Congressional support even as President Trump withholds approval of a $14 billion weapons package after meeting Xi Jinping. Analysts say the allocation demonstrates Congress values Taiwan defense against Chinese expansion.
